chapter: Banjo, piano and his own bands
title: Sam Hopkins, the Toyamas, Antoines and picnic jobs
summary: Interviewers ask for contact details of Sam Hopkins, Lawrence Eddergren and the Japanese banjoist; he talks about drummers Paul and Harold Antoine and picnic work.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

Yeah, sure. I got his phone number, his address. I'll give it to you before you go. Okay, yeah. I got them all in my book. Yeah. I got them all, man. All the musicians, you know a lot of them. Well, he gave me his name as Claiborne. Yeah, I know, but that's the book. The whole number is written 924 All-Inst Street. Yeah. Whenever I wanted him, I called him. 924. Yeah. I called him. He's coming back. He's coming back. Yeah. But I'd have to get rid of that drum player. You know?

Yeah, he's the one that I know the best. His name is Harold. Harold Antoine, yeah. I've seen everyone in a very long time.

Well, he played with me a couple of times because Paul couldn't play in the daytime with me. All our boys, see like Harold, well Harold would play any time. Harold, not a well guard but he could play. And Sammy Hopkins, well he can't play any day. We had a lot of picnics. We played on, you know, on Sundays, Sunday evenings around, say one o'clock, twelve o'clock in the day. We played in picnics, you know. But he couldn't play them jobs.
